name: Banwei (班味)
blurb: Chinese slang for the worn-out "office worker" look: tired eyes, haggard face, no energy
title: Banwei (班味) Meaning: Chinese Slang for the "Office Worker Look"
description: Banwei (班味), roughly "work smell", is Chinese slang for the tired eyes and haggard look people get from stressful jobs. It was a top Chinese buzzword of 2024.
answer: Banwei (班味, literally "shift smell" or "work vibe") is the worn-out look people take on after starting a job: tired eyes, a haggard face and a careless appearance, caused by heavy workloads, hard conditions and complicated office relationships. It took off thanks to an online essay titled 一旦上过班，你的气质就会改变了 (Once you have worked, your aura changes), which said that anyone who has had a job picks up this vibe and can never shake it. The word spread widely in 2024, spawned phrases like 去班味 (get rid of the work vibe), and made the 《咬文嚼字》 (Yaowen Jiaozi) list of the top ten Chinese buzzwords of 2024.

body: Banwei is not a real smell but an unmistakable "office worker" aura: dark circles, a blank stare, a numb expression, sloppy clothes and no energy even after hours. People compare their student photos with photos taken after a year of work and say the second one has "heavy banwei".
The tone is self-mocking. People use it to vent about burnout and to talk about keeping some room between work and life.

head: Date
Event
rows: The essay 一旦上过班，你的气质就会改变了 circulates, saying the tired look of working people "can't be faked"
班味 takes off across Chinese social media and short-video comment sections as people post their own
去班味 and 洗掉班味 (wash off the work vibe) become popular, with trips, vacations and exercise as "cures"
《咬文嚼字》 names 班味 No. 7 on its top ten buzzwords of 2024

ul: Self-mocking: "才上班半年，照片里的班味已经藏不住了。" (Six months into the job and the work vibe already shows in my photos.)
Weekend plans: "周末出去玩一趟，去去班味。" (A weekend trip to wash off the work vibe.)
On a photo: "这张证件照班味好重。" (This ID photo is pure office worker.)
As praise: "你一点班味都没有。" (You don't look like a tired office worker at all.)

faq.a: It spread from the online essay 一旦上过班，你的气质就会改变了 (Once you have worked, your aura changes), which said the tired look of working people sticks for good. People quickly adopted it as a joke about themselves.
"Getting rid of the work vibe": doing something that restores your energy, such as traveling, taking time off, exercising or seeing friends.

faq.q: Was banwei a word of the year?
faq.a: Yes. On 2 December 2024, the editors of 《咬文嚼字》 ranked 班味 No. 7 on their top ten buzzwords of 2024.
